references.text: Jesus elaborates in the same context on the warning that people will say, 'Look here!' or 'Look there!' regarding the coming of the Son of Man, which directly connects to Luke 17:21 where he says the kingdom of God does not come in a way that allows one to say, 'Look, it is here,' or 'There it is' (Luke 17:23).

Jesus says that when you see these things happening, you should know that the kingdom of God is near. This complements the thought in Luke 17:21 about the nearness and presence of the kingdom of God (Luke 21:31).

Jesus warns: 'If anyone then says to you, "Look, here is the Messiah," or "There he is," do not believe it.' The same warning against locating the kingdom of God or the Messiah in a specific place, parallel to Luke 17:21 (Mark 13:21).

Matthew's parallel to the warning about false claims regarding the presence of the Messiah: 'If anyone then says, "Look, here is the Messiah," or "There he is," do not believe it.' This connects to Jesus' point in Luke 17:21 that the kingdom does not come in an observable way (Matthew 24:23-26).

Jesus says: 'But if I drive out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.' This shows that the kingdom of God is already present among them, consistent with the idea that the kingdom is 'in your midst' (Luke 17:21) (Matthew 12:28).
Luke's parallel: 'But if I drive out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.' The kingdom of God is already at work among them, which supports Luke 17:21 (Luke 11:20).

Paul explains that 'the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking, but of righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.' This points to the inner and spiritual nature of the kingdom of God, which aligns with Jesus' words that the kingdom is 'in your midst' (Romans 14:17).
Jesus tells Pilate: 'My kingdom is not of this world.' The kingdom of God does not have an external, political character that one can point to, which harmonizes with Luke 17:21 (John 18:36).

Jesus says that no one can see the kingdom of God without being born again. The kingdom of God is not perceived through outward observation but through spiritual renewal—in line with Luke 17:21 (John 3:3).
Paul speaks of 'Christ in you, the hope of glory.' The inner presence of the kingdom of God in believers parallels Jesus' words that the kingdom of God is 'in your midst' (Colossians 1:27).
